title: ECONOMICS – INDIA & WORLD TRADE
subtitle: 100 practical questions on the Indian economy, taxation, RBI, trade and international economic organisations
source: Original syllabus-based questions with official reference metadata
verificationStatus: PRACTICE — official-source metadata; calculation and concept verification completed

questions.q: Which concept measures the final value of goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory during a period?
questions.explanation: GDP measures final output produced within the domestic territory over a specified period.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP:
questions.explanation: Real GDP uses constant prices, while nominal GDP uses current prices.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics
options: Uses base-year prices to adjust for inflation

questions.q: A rise in the general price level while quantities remain unchanged would generally:
questions.explanation: Higher prices increase the value measure of nominal GDP, while real GDP depends on constant-price quantities.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics
options: Raise nominal GDP but not necessarily real GDP

questions.q: Per capita income is calculated by dividing national income or output by:
questions.explanation: Per capita income relates aggregate income or output to the population.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: Economic development differs from economic growth because development also includes:
questions.explanation: Development is broader and considers improvements in welfare and human capabilities.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics
options: Living standards, health and social welfare

questions.q: Agriculture and allied activities generally belong to the:
questions.explanation: The primary sector directly uses natural resources, including agriculture.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: Manufacturing most clearly belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Manufacturing converts raw or intermediate products into finished goods.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: A firm with no formal registration or accounting records is most likely to operate in the:
questions.explanation: Informality is characterised by limited or absent formal registration and regulated employment/accounting arrangements.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: The public sector mainly consists of:
questions.explanation: Public-sector units are owned or controlled by central, state or local governments.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total government expenditure over:
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit measures borrowing requirement and equals expenditure over receipts excluding borrowings.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: Revenue deficit arises when:
questions.explanation: Revenue deficit compares revenue expenditure with revenue receipts.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: If national income is ₹1,00,000 crore and population is 25 crore, national income per person is:
questions.explanation: Divide 1,00,000 crore by 25 crore: ₹4000 per person.
questions.sourceName: Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.sourceDescription: National accounts and Indian economic statistics

questions.q: A tax is compulsory payment to government and ordinarily:
questions.explanation: Tax is a compulsory contribution made for public expenditure without a direct individual return.
options: Does not provide an individual-specific quid pro quo
Creates an individual debt equal to benefits received

questions.q: Income tax is primarily a:
questions.explanation: Income tax is paid directly by the taxpayer on taxable income.

questions.q: GST paid at the point of purchase is generally:
questions.explanation: GST is levied on supply and collected in the transaction chain rather than directly assessed on personal income.

questions.q: Corporate tax is levied on:
questions.explanation: Corporate tax applies to taxable company income/profits under direct-tax law.

questions.q: Capital gains tax applies to profit arising from:
questions.explanation: Capital gains are changes resulting from transfer of qualifying capital assets.

questions.q: TDS is:
questions.explanation: TDS is withheld by the person making specified payments and remitted to the tax authority.
options: Tax deducted by payer and deposited to government
Tax paid only at year-end by every taxpayer

questions.q: TCS ordinarily means:
questions.explanation: TCS requires specified sellers/collectors to collect tax on covered transactions.
options: Tax collected at source on specified transactions

questions.q: The old and new income-tax regimes differ mainly in:
questions.explanation: The regimes apply different provisions on slabs and eligible deductions/exemptions.
options: Available deductions/exemptions and applicable slab structures
Whether income tax is a direct tax

questions.q: A tax deduction from taxable income generally:
questions.explanation: A lawful deduction reduces the taxable base, subject to eligibility conditions.
options: Reduces taxable income if conditions are met

questions.q: An exemption in direct tax means:
questions.explanation: Exemption excludes qualifying income or transactions from taxable scope under the governing provision.
options: The specified income or category is excluded from tax under the law
The taxpayer pays no customs duty only
The tax authority waives all future tax

questions.q: Tax evasion is:
questions.explanation: Tax evasion uses illegal concealment or misstatement rather than lawful planning.
options: Illegal concealment or understatement to avoid tax

questions.q: Tax avoidance differs from evasion because avoidance:
questions.explanation: Avoidance is within the legal framework; evasion involves unlawful concealment or misrepresentation.
options: Uses legally permissible provisions to reduce tax

questions.q: A progressive tax is one in which:
questions.explanation: Progressive taxation increases the applicable rate or burden with ability to pay.
options: Higher income groups generally face a higher marginal rate
The same fixed amount applies to everyone

questions.q: A proportional tax charges:
questions.explanation: Proportional tax uses a constant rate on the relevant tax base.
options: The same rate on the taxable base
A higher rate at every income level
Different rates depending on customs origin

questions.q: A regressive tax can mean:
questions.explanation: A regressive burden is relatively heavier for lower-income taxpayers.
options: Its burden takes a larger share of lower incomes
It always has a rising marginal rate
It is not paid as money

questions.q: Income tax is generally administered as a:
questions.explanation: Income tax other than agricultural income is levied by the Union.

questions.q: A salaried person receives ₹50,000 and has a lawful deduction of ₹5,000. Taxable salary for that simple illustration is:
questions.explanation: Taxable salary is ₹50,000 minus the ₹5,000 deduction, giving ₹45,000.

questions.q: Tax revenue contributes mainly to:
questions.explanation: Tax revenue finances public goods and government programmes.

questions.q: GST is a tax on:
questions.explanation: GST is levied on specified supplies of goods or services.

questions.q: For a supply within one Indian state, CGST and SGST generally apply instead of IGST:
questions.explanation: An intra-state supply ordinarily attracts CGST and SGST; IGST applies to inter-state supplies.

questions.q: Goods sold from Maharashtra to Uttar Pradesh are ordinarily:
questions.explanation: Cross-state supply is inter-state and ordinarily attracts IGST.
options: An intra-state supply attracting only CGST

questions.q: Input Tax Credit allows a registered taxpayer to:
questions.explanation: ITC offsets eligible taxes paid on inputs against GST output liability, subject to conditions.
options: Set eligible input tax against output tax liability
Receive a refund in every case

questions.q: GST registration becomes relevant when:
questions.explanation: Registration depends on business liability, threshold and mandatory provisions.
options: A person meets applicable threshold or mandatory registration conditions
A person makes any personal purchase
Only a bank account is opened

questions.q: A GST invoice primarily provides:
questions.explanation: A GST invoice records supply and tax details required for invoicing and input tax credit.
options: Supply, tax and party details for compliance

questions.q: The GST Council is responsible for:
questions.explanation: The GST Council includes Union and State representation and recommends GST policy.
options: Recommendations on GST policy and structure

questions.q: GST collection is deposited by:
questions.explanation: Registered taxable persons collect GST and remit it through the GST system.
options: Registered suppliers through the GST framework
Only State treasuries directly from consumers

questions.q: Customs duty is imposed primarily on:
questions.explanation: Customs duty regulates and taxes specified goods crossing customs borders.
options: Cross-border import or export of specified goods

questions.q: Import duty generally:
questions.explanation: Import duty is part of the landed-cost burden on specified imports.
options: Adds to the cost of an imported product
Is only a corporate income tax

questions.q: Export duty is:
questions.explanation: Export duty applies to selected goods exported outside India.
options: A customs duty on specified exports
A tax on only inter-state domestic sales

questions.q: CGST is the component collected for:
questions.explanation: CGST represents the Central Government share on intra-state supplies.
options: The Union share on an intra-state GST supply

questions.q: The Union Budget presents:
questions.explanation: The Union Budget sets proposed government revenue and expenditure.
options: Government receipts and proposed expenditure for the financial year

questions.q: Tax receipts are an example of:
questions.explanation: Tax revenue is recurring and generally classified as revenue receipt.

questions.q: Loan recovery by government is normally:
questions.explanation: Loan recoveries are asset-related inflows and form capital receipts.

questions.q: Building a bridge is usually:
questions.explanation: Creation or acquisition of an asset is generally capital expenditure.

questions.q: Salaries paid to regular public officials are generally:
questions.explanation: Recurring employee compensation is revenue expenditure.

questions.q: A subsidy is:
questions.explanation: Subsidies transfer resources to reduce specified costs or support policy objectives.
options: Government financial support to reduce a cost or price

questions.q: Infrastructure spending is often treated as:
questions.explanation: Infrastructure spending is public investment in physical or social assets.
options: Public investment that creates assets or capacity

questions.q: Government borrowing increases:
questions.explanation: Borrowing creates a liability that becomes part of public debt.

questions.q: The Union Budget is presented by:
questions.explanation: The Union Finance Minister presents the Union Budget on behalf of the government.
options: The Ministry of Finance / Union Finance Minister
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade

questions.q: If expenditure is ₹100 crore and receipts excluding borrowing are ₹90 crore, fiscal deficit is:
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = expenditure minus receipts excluding borrowing: ₹100 crore minus ₹90 crore = ₹10 crore.

questions.q: The RBI is India's:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India is the country's central bank.

questions.q: When the RBI raises the repo rate, commercial banks may face:
questions.explanation: Repo-rate increases raise costs for secured short-term central-bank borrowing and can transmit to lending rates.
options: Higher short-term borrowing costs and potentially higher lending rates

questions.q: CRR refers to:
questions.explanation: CRR is the minimum portion of specified bank liabilities that banks maintain as central-bank cash reserve.

questions.q: SLR requires banks to maintain a proportion of specified liabilities in:
questions.explanation: Statutory Liquidity Ratio requires maintenance in approved liquid assets.
options: Approved liquid assets such as government securities and cash

questions.q: Monetary policy mainly uses instruments to influence:
questions.explanation: Monetary policy seeks to manage liquidity and monetary conditions.

questions.q: If food, fuel and other representative consumer prices rise broadly and persistently, the economy is experiencing:
questions.explanation: Broad, sustained increases in consumer prices indicate inflation.

questions.q: Deflation means:
questions.explanation: Deflation is a broad, sustained decline in prices.
options: A sustained decrease in the general price level
A loss of foreign reserves only

questions.q: CPI is used especially to track:
questions.explanation: Consumer Price Index measures changes in a representative consumer basket.
options: Changes in consumer goods and services prices

questions.q: WPI primarily measures:
questions.explanation: Wholesale Price Index tracks prices at the wholesale stage.

questions.q: The bank rate is:
questions.explanation: Bank rate is an RBI policy/reference rate for designated central-bank lending windows.
options: A rate at which RBI lends to banks under applicable RBI facilities
The interest on every savings deposit

questions.q: Financial inclusion aims to:
questions.explanation: Financial inclusion expands access to appropriate financial services.
options: Provide usable and affordable financial services to underserved people

questions.q: If policy interest rates rise for a borrower on a floating-rate loan, monthly interest cost generally:
questions.explanation: A floating-rate loan linked to a rising benchmark usually has a higher interest cost.
options: Increases if the loan rate is fully linked and benchmarked

questions.q: An import is:
questions.explanation: Imports enter the domestic economy from foreign sources.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Purchase of a good or service from abroad
Sale of a domestic good abroad

questions.q: An export is:
questions.explanation: Exports are sold to buyers outside the domestic economy.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Sale of domestic goods or services to foreign buyers

questions.q: Why does India import substantial crude oil?
questions.explanation: India depends materially on crude imports for petroleum product demand.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Domestic production is insufficient to meet refinery and fuel demand
Crude oil cannot be used in India

questions.q: Major Indian exports include:
questions.explanation: India exports a diversified range, including medicines, textiles and services.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Pharmaceutical products, textiles and IT services

questions.q: Major Indian imports include:
questions.explanation: India imports energy and capital/consumer products in significant categories.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data

questions.q: Merchandise trade concerns:
questions.explanation: Merchandise trade refers to physical goods; services trade is separately classified.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data

questions.q: A trade deficit occurs when merchandise imports exceed merchandise exports:
questions.explanation: The merchandise trade deficit is the excess of merchandise imports over exports.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data

questions.q: India may have a trade deficit even while:
questions.explanation: The trade and services/current-account balances are separate but related components.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data

questions.q: A tariff is:
questions.explanation: Tariffs alter the price of traded goods through customs duties.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: A tax on imported or sometimes exported goods
A subsidy paid to every consumer

questions.q: A non-tariff barrier can include:
questions.explanation: Non-tariff barriers regulate trade without an ordinary tariff.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data

questions.q: Export incentives may aim to:
questions.explanation: Export incentives include schemes supporting competitiveness and specified exports.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Improve export competitiveness or promote specified sectors

questions.q: Ports and logistics improve trade by:
questions.explanation: Efficient ports and logistics move goods faster and at lower delivered cost.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Reducing transport delay and transaction cost

questions.q: International trade creates jobs primarily through:
questions.explanation: Trade expands production and service employment across export and logistics chains.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data
options: Export industries, logistics and related services

questions.q: If imports cost $200 million and exports earn $170 million, the merchandise trade deficit is:
questions.explanation: Merchandise trade deficit equals imports minus exports: 200 minus 170 = $30 million.
questions.sourceDescription: Foreign trade policy and trade data

questions.q: The United States is strategically important for India primarily because of:
questions.explanation: India has extensive trade, technology and services links with the US.

questions.q: China is a major source for India of:
questions.explanation: China supplies varied manufactured and intermediate products to India.
options: Machinery and electronics among other goods

questions.q: The UAE is important in India–West Asia trade because it is:
questions.explanation: The UAE is a major trade, logistics and energy-related partner for India.
options: A major commercial and re-export hub and energy trade partner
An inland neighbour with no ports

questions.q: Russia remains strategically relevant to India’s trade due in part to:
questions.explanation: Russia has commercial links with India spanning energy and strategic sectors.
options: Energy, defence and strategic commodities trade

questions.q: Saudi Arabia is significant for India mainly because of:
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia is an important energy supplier and investment/commerce partner.

questions.q: Singapore is important for India as:
questions.explanation: Singapore supports trade, shipping and regional financial and commercial links.
options: A trade, logistics and financial-services hub

questions.q: The European Union is for trade purposes:
questions.explanation: The EU is a 27-member economic and political union with a coordinated trade policy.
options: A grouping of 27 European member states

questions.q: Japan is closely relevant to India through:
questions.explanation: Japan and India cooperate across technology, investment and infrastructure.

questions.q: Bangladesh is an important trade partner for India mainly due to:
questions.explanation: India and Bangladesh conduct substantial regional trade across a shared border.

questions.q: Australia is relevant to India’s trade and resources because of:
questions.explanation: Australia has growing trade, resources and education/services links with India.
options: Economic, critical minerals and services cooperation

questions.q: The WTO sets rules and provides a forum for:
questions.explanation: The WTO administers trade agreements and dispute settlement.
questions.sourceName: World Trade Organization / IMF / World Bank
options: Multilateral international trade negotiations and dispute settlement
Only customs duty collection in India

questions.q: The IMF primarily assists members with:
questions.explanation: The IMF provides surveillance and financial support for balance-of-payments difficulties.
questions.sourceName: World Trade Organization / IMF / World Bank
options: Balance-of-payments support and economic policy surveillance

questions.q: The World Bank group mainly provides:
questions.explanation: World Bank institutions support development through finance and knowledge.
questions.sourceName: World Trade Organization / IMF / World Bank

questions.q: The Asian Development Bank supports:
questions.explanation: ADB provides development finance and technical support in Asia.
questions.sourceName: World Trade Organization / IMF / World Bank
options: Economic development and regional cooperation in Asia

questions.q: BRICS is:
questions.explanation: BRICS is a cooperation forum involving Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.
questions.sourceName: World Trade Organization / IMF / World Bank
options: A multilateral economic and political cooperation grouping
A customs union for Indian states

questions.q: An FTA mainly seeks to:
questions.explanation: Free trade agreements reduce tariffs or barriers under negotiated rules.
questions.sourceName: World Trade Organization / IMF / World Bank
options: Reduce or eliminate specified trade barriers among participants

questions.q: An exchange rate is:
questions.explanation: Exchange rate specifies how many units of one currency exchange for another.
questions.sourceDescription: Exchange rates, reserves and balance of payments
options: The price of one currency in terms of another

questions.q: If the rupee depreciates against the dollar while the dollar price of crude oil is unchanged, India's crude import bill in rupees generally:
questions.explanation: The same dollar outlay requires more rupees when the rupee depreciates.
questions.sourceDescription: Exchange rates, reserves and balance of payments

questions.q: Rupee depreciation can make Indian exports:
questions.explanation: Depreciation can lower the foreign-currency price of domestic exports, subject to costs and demand.
questions.sourceDescription: Exchange rates, reserves and balance of payments
options: Potentially more competitive in foreign-currency terms

questions.q: Foreign exchange reserves are:
questions.explanation: Forex reserves are external assets held to support monetary and external-sector stability.
questions.sourceDescription: Exchange rates, reserves and balance of payments
options: Foreign assets held by the central bank and public-authority institutions

questions.q: FDI differs from FPI mainly because FDI:
questions.explanation: Foreign direct investment reflects a lasting interest and influence/control; FPI is portfolio investment.
questions.sourceDescription: Exchange rates, reserves and balance of payments
options: Usually involves lasting interest and control in an enterprise

questions.q: An ₹80 crore export receipt is converted at ₹83 per US dollar. Approximately how many million US dollars are received?
questions.explanation: Divide ₹800 million by ₹83 per dollar, giving approximately USD 9.6386 million.
questions.sourceDescription: Exchange rates, reserves and balance of payments
